clue.text: Chances rum sling to start with

parts.note: rum in its old sense of strange or peculiar

indicators.note: what comes to start with is the opening letter only of the word just before

parts.note: the initial letter of sling

explanation.surface: Someone weighing their chances of trouble after a rum sling cocktail or two.
explanation.walkthrough: A rum sling looks like a drink, but rum is the adjective for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: The odds on something are its probability or likelihood of happening, its chances.

clue.text: Bizarre sound lathi makes when swished

indicators.note: a stick swished through the air is whirled about, so its letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; a lathi is an Indian iron-bound bamboo stick

explanation.surface: A strange whooshing noise made by a heavy Indian stick swung through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlandish means strikingly strange or unfamiliar, a close synonym of weird or bizarre.

clue.text: Don't exaggerate attraction over Italian beer

parts.note: a draw is something that pulls in crowds
IT is the standard abbreviation for Italian
mild is a dark, lightly hopped British ale

explanation.surface: Advice not to overstate the appeal of a pint of Italian lager.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, A over B puts A above, so before, B. Mild is a traditional style of British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom urging someone to moderate their claims is an imperative, just like the phrase in the clue.

clue.text: Wrote about bar in high-rise building

indicators.note: about can mean in a roundabout way, so the preceding word's letters are moved around

parts.note: its letters rearranged
to bar something is to block it

explanation.surface: Someone wrote about a pub found in a tall apartment building.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower block is a tall residential or office building, the British term for a high-rise.

clue.text: Recorded short, readily available

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: recorded material is on tape

explanation.surface: A recording kept brief and so easy to get hold of.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer on tap is drawn straight from the cask, so the idiom means available whenever needed.

clue.text: Exterminate last of those spread out round Cape

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter alone

parts.note: the final letter of those

indicators.note: one part goes round another, enclosing it

parts.note: to radiate is to spread out from a centre
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: An order to wipe out the stragglers scattered about a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: E plus RADIATE makes ERADIATE, which then wraps around C.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to destroy completely, root and branch, the same as exterminating.

clue.text: Expose band, very briefly, to harm outside

indicators.note: one word sits outside the others, wrapping around them

parts.note: a blight is something that damages or spoils

indicators.note: kept brief, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a ring is a circular band
too means very, as in not too happy

explanation.surface: A musical group is exposed, quickly, to damage from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Very briefly is one instruction: a word for very, cut short. The surface reads band as musicians, but it is a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something to light is to reveal or uncover it, an idiomatic way of saying expose.

clue.text: No starter for joint in oven

indicators.note: without its starter, the word drops its opening letter

parts.note: a roast is a joint of meat

explanation.surface: A cook's warning that a starter is off because the joint is still roasting.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is a kiln for drying hops, a familiar sight in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast is a kiln, a kind of oven used to dry hops for brewing.

clue.text: Knockout girl wanting ring

parts.note: Kay is a girl's name
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A stunning young woman hoping for an engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Knockout and ring tempt the solver towards boxing, which the answer does deliver.
explanation.definitionFit: Kayo is a spelled-out form of KO, the abbreviation for a boxing knockout.

clue.text: Vagrant drops penny in vehicle

indicators.note: dropping something means it is left out of the word

parts.note: a tramp is a homeless wanderer
P is the abbreviation for penny, the one dropped

explanation.surface: A homeless person loses a coin while riding public transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a passenger vehicle running on rails along city streets.

clue.text: Navy skirts excited composer

indicators.note: excited means agitated, so the letters before are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sailors' uniforms getting a composer worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Skirts looks like a verb meaning goes round, but it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor Stravinsky was the Russian composer of The Rite of Spring.

clue.text: Archbishop's line into Aldgate, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bishop who heads an ecclesiastical province
second meaning: the London Underground line with a terminus at Aldgate

explanation.surface: A senior cleric's route into a district of the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Aldgate is a London Underground station at the end of the Metropolitan line; perhaps marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: In church usage a metropolitan is the archbishop presiding over a province; the Tube line bears the same name.

clue.text: Girl's brought across bound for an Australian town

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name
to bound is to leap, or spring

explanation.surface: A girl is carried over the sea, heading for somewhere in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Bound looks like heading for, but it is the verb to leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice Springs is the town in the middle of Australia's Northern Territory.

clue.text: Fly low? Nerve's required

parts.note: to feel blue is to feel low
bottle is British slang for courage

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether flying low takes courage.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle meaning nerve or guts is everyday British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebottle is a large blowfly with a metallic blue body.

clue.text: Article on domestic film

parts.note: the definite article
a domestic is a household servant

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a homegrown movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Domestic looks like an adjective for film, but it is the noun for a household servant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Servant is Joseph Losey's 1963 British film starring Dirk Bogarde as a sinister manservant.

clue.text: Slightly reduced, modest object

indicators.note: reduced a little means trimmed by just one letter at the end

parts.note: demure means shy and modest

explanation.surface: A modest little item, made a bit smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: Object reads as a noun, but it is the verb, to raise an objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise doubts or objections, so it can stand for the verb object.

clue.text: Religious leader at a holy resort around LA

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the last piece, enclosing it
to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters before are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleric visits a sacred holiday destination somewhere near Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: Resort looks like a holiday spot, but read as re-sort it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior Shia Muslim cleric, especially in Iran.

clue.text: Militant reformers visit cast unexpectedly

indicators.note: something done unexpectedly comes out in an unforeseen arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Protesters turn up without warning to see the actors of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Activists campaign vigorously for political or social change, often taking direct action.

clue.text: Sailor safe, reportedly, after using explosive ingredient

parts.note: an old salt is an experienced sailor

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: peter is old underworld slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A seaman cracks a safe using explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is thieves' slang for a safe, so a safecracker is a peterman.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is the oxidising ingredient in gunpowder.

clue.text: A side changed plans

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters before take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A team altered its strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas can mean intentions or schemes, as in having ideas of moving abroad.

clue.text: Last minute of a sixty-minute period

definitions.text: Last minute of a sixty-minute period

parts.note: surface reading: the final sixty seconds of an hour
setter's reading: the last moment, named after one of the twelve hourly periods of a clock day

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the 60th minute of an hour; the answer is an idiom for the last possible moment, which is itself named as an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, from the parable of the labourers in the vineyard, means the latest possible time before it is too late.

clue.text: Trap quickly set up by base of tree

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means raised so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: soon means without delay

indicators.note: the base of a word in a down clue is its bottom, final letter

parts.note: the final letter of tree

explanation.surface: A snare rigged in haste at the foot of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop with a running knot used as a snare for animals.

clue.text: Bishop in group

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a title given to bishops in the Syriac and Coptic churches
second meaning: the Swedish pop group of Waterloo fame

explanation.surface: A churchman plays in a band.
explanation.definitionFit: Abba, Aramaic for father, is a title for bishops in Eastern churches, and also the name of a famous Swedish pop group.

clue.text: Ranch a great distance away? Miles

parts.note: far means a long way off
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: A homestead so remote it is miles from anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Miles looks like the answer to the question, but it is just the M.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one raising cattle in the Americas.

clue.text: Odd types about pointing to mole

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters that follow are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Strange characters gesture towards a burrowing animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Mole looks like the animal or a spy, but it is the small dark mark on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty spot is a small dark mark on the face, natural or painted on, like a mole.

clue.text: Greek leaves Scottish village for high peak

indicators.note: what leaves is taken away from the word that remains

parts.note: Gretna, the border village famous for runaway weddings
GR is the abbreviation for Greek

explanation.surface: A Greek traveller swaps a Scottish village for a mountain holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Gretna (Green) is the Scottish border village once famous for runaway marriages.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the tall active volcano on Sicily, the highest peak in Italy south of the Alps.

clue.text: Notice clergyman's in control

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A sign says the vicar is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer is to manage or run affairs, which is to control them.

clue.text: Worst, or just the opposite?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the verb to worst, to defeat
second meaning: the superlative contrary to worst

explanation.walkthrough: Worst seems to be the superlative of bad, but here it is the verb to defeat, and the answer as a verb means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to get the better of them, as to worst them is; as adjectives the two are opposites.
